title: Local cohomological dimension: generator and proper-sum bounds
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For a finitely generated ideal $K$ of a ring $A$, write $H_K^j(M)=R^j\Gamma_K(M)$, using [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor], where $\Gamma_K(M)=\{x\in M:K^nx=0\text{ for some }n\}$, and let $\operatorname{cd}(A,K)$ be the least integer $q\geq-1$ such that $H_K^j(M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ and every $j>q$. For every proper finitely generated ideal $I$ generated by $r\geq0$ elements, $0\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)\leq r$. If $I,J$ are finitely generated ideals with $I+J\ne A$, then $\operatorname{cd}(A,I+J)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)+\operatorname{cd}(A,J)$. In particular, if $f_1,\ldots,f_e\in A$ and $I+(f_1,\ldots,f_e)\ne A$, then $\operatorname{cd}(A,I+(f_1,\ldots,f_e))\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)+e$.

source.place: Tag 0DX8 (definition-cd), Tag 0DX7 (lemma-cd), Tag 0DX9 (lemma-bound-cd), and Tag 0ECP (lemma-cd-sum), restricted to proper sums.

proof.text: Choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ of $I$ and apply [lem-per-local-cohomology-cech-bound] over the Noetherian ring $A$ to every module $M$. Its complex has zero terms in degrees $j>r$, so $H_I^j(M)=0$ for all such $j$. Thus the set of integer bounds $q\geq-1$ in the statement is nonempty and has a least member, with $\operatorname{cd}(A,I)\leq r$. This proves existence and the upper bound. The same argument gives a finite bound for every finitely generated ideal, whether proper or not. If $r=0$, the cited model is just $M[0]$, so the conclusion still holds.

For a proper ideal $I$, the module $A/I$ is nonzero and is killed by $I$. Hence $\Gamma_I(A/I)=A/I$ by [def-sbc-ideal-power-torsion-functor]. Also $H_I^0(N)=\Gamma_I(N)$: in an injective resolution $0\to N\to E^0\to E^1$, the kernel after taking the torsion submodules is exactly the torsion submodule of the original kernel $N$. Consequently $H_I^0(A/I)\ne0$, and $-1$ cannot be a bound. Together with Step 1 this proves $0\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)\leq r$.

source.place: Tag 0DX7 (lemma-cd), proof for d=-1, and Tag 0DX8 (definition-cd).

proof.text: Suppose $I+J\ne A$. Then both $I$ and $J$ are proper; by Steps 1–2 put $a=\operatorname{cd}(A,I)\geq0$ and $b=\operatorname{cd}(A,J)\geq0$. Apply [lem-per-local-cohomology-sum-spectral] to an arbitrary module $M$, with $E_2^{p,q}=H_I^p(H_J^q(M))$. If $p>a$, this is zero because the bound for $I$ holds for every module, including $H_J^q(M)$; if $q>b$, the inner module is zero. For $n>a+b$, every pair $p,q\geq0$ with $p+q=n$ therefore has zero $E_2^{p,q}$, and its later pages, being subquotients, remain zero. The cited finite filtration of $H_{I+J}^n(M)$ has only zero graded pieces, so this group is zero. Since $M$ was arbitrary, the defining least-bound property gives $\operatorname{cd}(A,I+J)\leq a+b$.

source.place: Tag 0ECP (lemma-cd-sum), restricted to proper sums; dualizing.tex Tags 0BJC (lemma-local-cohomology-ss) and 0955.

proof.text: Put $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_e)$. Properness of $I+J$ implies properness of both summands. Step 1 applied to this $e$-generated ideal $J$ gives $\operatorname{cd}(A,J)\leq e$. Substitute this in Step 3 to obtain $\operatorname{cd}(A,I+J)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)+\operatorname{cd}(A,J)\leq\operatorname{cd}(A,I)+e$, the asserted final clause. If $e=0$, then $J=0$, whose cohomology is concentrated in degree zero by Step 1's empty-list model, and the same calculation applies.

source.place: Tags 0DX9 (lemma-bound-cd)(1) and 0ECP (lemma-cd-sum), elementary substitution of Steps 1 and 3.

lean.statement: theorem localCohomology_generator_bound (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Nontrivial A] [IsNoetherianRing A] : (∀ (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A), I = Ideal.span (Set.range f) → I ≠ ⊤ → 0 ≤ localCohomologicalDimension I ∧ localCohomologicalDimension I ≤ r) ∧ (∀ (I J : Ideal A), I.FG → J.FG → I + J ≠ ⊤ → localCohomologicalDimension (I + J) ≤ localCohomologicalDimension I + localCohomologicalDimension J) ∧ (∀ (I : Ideal A) (e : ℕ) (f : Fin e → A), I.FG → I + Ideal.span (Set.range f) ≠ ⊤ → localCohomologicalDimension (I + Ideal.span (Set.range f)) ≤ localCohomologicalDimension I + e)
